Vertex permutations preserve area and the equal-length vertex vectors sum to zero, so equal positive weights give the required area-weighted balance.

The regular tetrahedron's vertex vectors span R³ and have a one-dimensional dependence space generated by the all-ones vector. Hence the four normal vectors form a minimal positive dependence. The homothety x↦v_i+(3/4)(x−v_i) maps the tetrahedron onto the positive cap λ_i≥1/4 and scales volume by 27/64.

For any competing menu discard zero-weight terms and translate the interior source to zero. Extend its positive-weight normal span to a two-plane E. An interior ball projects to a disk, section centroids project to zero, and through-origin sections, their areas, and weighted balance match the accepted theorem's conventions.

At d=3 the square-root term √(4/3) is at most 4/3, giving c₃=3/7. Exact subtraction gives 3/7−27/64=3/448>0. The gap applies with a changed body in the same ambient dimension and is compatible with reductions restricted to strict violations of 27/64.
